newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to consolidate after record close.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to consolidate after record close.

text.p: The Brussels' Bel-20 share index ended at a fifth record high on Monday, recovering from falls in early trade amid media allegations that government minister Elio Di Rupo was linked to a sex scandal.
Profit taking also weighed on the market, dealers said.
"We will now have to face weeks of consolidation, and if the economic recovery continues in Europe, there is room for the index to rise further," said a dealer.
Some dealers said the allegations against Di Rupo -- who is a member of the core cabinet -- had only affected the index in early trading.

The Bel-20 ended up 2.69 points or 0.14 percent, at 1,872.17, above its previous all-time high of 1,869.48 set on Friday. Dealers said the steady rise in the Dow Jones index .DJI and low interest rates lured new buyers into the market.
Some dealers said the bourse could still reach 1,900 by the new year, after a period of consolidation.
But the morning saw a volatile bourse with investors looking to consolidate their positions.
Dealers said institutional investors were the predominant sellers while small-scale individual investors were still picking up stocks.
Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere fell 2.65 percent to 2,200 francs.
Dealers were surprised at its fall, saying most of the stock sold was from a large institutional seller.
Metal construction company Bekaert faced similar profit-taking, dropping 0.66 percent to 26,325 francs, as did insurer Royale Belge. It ended down 0.58 percent at 6,800 francs.
Steel-maker Cockerill CCK_pt.BR fell another 1.7 percent to 117 francs, continuing a spell of poor performance.
